original_value: In the scenario where autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) carry out tasks, it is necessary to reliably estimate underwater-moving-target positioning. While cameras often give low-precision visibility in a limited field of view, the forward-looking sonar is still an attractive method for underwater sensing, which is especially effective for long-range tracking. This paper describes an online processing framework based on forward-looking-sonar (FLS) images, and presents a novel tracking approach based on a Gaussian particle filter (GPF) to resolve persistent multiple-target tracking in cluttered environments. First, the character of acoustic-vision images is considered, and methods of median filtering and region-growing segmentation were modified to improve image-processing results. Second, a generalized regression neural network was adopted to evaluate multiple features of target regions, and a representation of feature subsets was created to improve tracking performance. Thus, an adaptive fusion strategy is introduced to integrate feature cues into the observation model, and the complete procedure of underwater target tracking based on GPF is displayed. Results obtained on a real acoustic-vision AUV platform during sea trials are shown and discussed. These showed that the proposed method is feasible and effective in tracking targets in complex underwater environments.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents an online processing framework built from forward-looking sonar (FLS) images and a new Gaussian particle filter (GPF)-based tracking method for persistent multi-target tracking in cluttered underwater environments. In scenarios where autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs) perform tasks, reliable estimation of underwater moving-target positions is required. Although cameras typically provide low-precision visibility over a limited field of view, forward-looking sonar remains an appealing sensing approach, especially for long-range tracking. To improve image processing, the acoustic-vision image characteristics were taken into account and the median filtering and region-growing segmentation methods were adapted. A generalized regression neural network was then used to assess multiple features of target regions, and feature-subset representations were formed to enhance tracking performance. An adaptive fusion strategy integrates the feature cues into the observation model, and the full GPF-based underwater target-tracking procedure is presented. Experiments on a real acoustic-vision AUV platform during sea trials are reported and discussed, showing that the proposed approach is feasible and effective for tracking targets in complex underwater environments.
